title: Development of novel pyrazolyl thiazole hybrids: synthesis and antiproliferative evaluation with  in silico  investigation of VEGFR-2 binding
content: A series of pyrazolyl-thiazole derivatives was synthesized from 3,5-dimethyl-4-(phenyldiazenyl)-1H-pyrazole-1-carbothioamide using hydrazonoyl halides and α-halo compounds, together with a derivative obtained using dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate. The products were characterized by spectroscopic and analytical methods and evaluated against HCT-116 human colorectal cancer cells using a 24 h MTT assay. Compounds 4a–c, 10, 12, and 16 gave IC50 values of 5.16 ± 1.33–7.51 ± 1.52 µM, compared with 7.18 ± 0.44 µM for doxorubicin. These comparisons are descriptive and do not establish statistically significant superiority. The six selected compounds had reported IC50 values >100 µM in non-tumor LLC-MK2 cells, yielding preliminary lower-bound selectivity estimates. This cross-species, cross-tissue comparison does not establish cancer-specific selectivity or absence of toxicity. Docking against VEGFR-2 produced scores of −8.3 to −11.6 kcal mol−1; compound 16 had the lowest mean HCT-116 IC50 and the most negative docking score. Across the 14 final products, the association between docking score and pIC50 was not statistically significant (Spearman ρ = −0.370, two-sided p = 0.193). The findings support further investigation of the series, particularly compound 16. However, MTT measures metabolic activity indirectly, and biochemical target validation, additional human non-tumor models, and longer-duration cellular studies are needed before drawing mechanistic or therapeutic conclusions.
